subject: SLA & escalation retainer — proposed uptime bands, credits, and discount request
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@nimbushealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aaron Silva <aaron.silva@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify SLA bands + escalation coverage (RFI attached)

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're putting together the procurement packet and need clearer language on your SLA tiers, escalation coverage, and how service credits would be calculated. A few specific asks: 

- Can you confirm uptime tiers you offer (hosted vs dedicated) and typical median/95th/99th latency targets?
- What is your P1/P2/P3 response-time commitment and on-call escalation rotation?
- How do you calculate downtime for rolling upgrades vs actual outage?
- Do you offer a retainer/premium support add-on that includes 24/7 on-call for named contacts? If so, what are the costs and is there a volume discount for committed spend?

I've attached an SLA_RFI.xlsx with fields our procurement team uses. We're targeting an initial annual committed spend range of $300k–$600k depending on pricing and credits. We may ask legal for tighter credits if the service is core to our customer flows.

Can you get us an initial proposal by Wednesday EOD PST?

—Olivia
Director of Platform Engineering
Nimbus Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify SLA bands + escalation coverage (RFI attached)

Olivia —

Thanks for the detailed RFI and the range; helpful context. Looping in Vivek (solutions) and Laura (accounts) so we can put a succinct proposal together. Quick answers up front and we'll follow with a short options PDF: 

- Uptime bands (hosted): 99.9% (standard), 99.95% (premium). For Dedicated we can offer 99.95% standard, 99.99% for committed annual contracts with capacity reservations.
- Response times (typical proposal):
  • P1 (production down / severe): acknowledge within 15 min, engineer engaged within 1 hour, 24/7 on-call for premium retainer customers.
  • P2 (degraded): ack within 1 hour, next-business-hour engineer engagement for standard support.
  • P3 (non-urgent): next-business-day triage.
- Downtime calculation: we exclude scheduled maintenance windows with ≥48h notice; rolling model upgrades that don’t impact traffic routing are not counted as downtime. We can provide a clearer definition in the SLA doc.

We can also offer a premium escalation retainer that provides: named primary/secondary support engineers, guaranteed 4-hour remediation SLAs for P1 for Dedicated customers, and a playbook for priority escalation to engineering leadership. For committed spend above $500k/yr we can discuss a support retainer discount (ballpark 10% on the retainer; final pricing depends on term and capacity).

I'll attach a short deck with three packaging options and proposed credits structure by band. If that aligns, Laura can open a formal quote in HubSpot and we can loop legal for a clean SLA text.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Olivia —

Adding a few technical clarifications from the ops side that we should call out explicitly in the SLA draft: 

1) What counts as outage: Any complete inability to reach the inference endpoint (500/502/503 across > 5% of requests measured at the edge for > 5 continuous minutes) will be treated as downtime. Transient client errors and user-specific failures are excluded.

2) Rolling upgrades: Our control plane supports draining and routing to healthy replicas; unless traffic is involuntarily dropped above the threshold above, those windows are not downtime. We'll provide a maintenance calendar and a template 48h notice mechanism.

3) Escalation runbook: For retainer customers we assign a named technical lead + secondary; the lead is paged on P1s immediately with an expectation of on-call acknowledgement in 15 minutes and triage call within 60 minutes. For Hosted (non-retainer) customers, we provide business-hours coverage with after-hours escalation to on-call engineering only for P1s.

4) Credits model (proposal):
  • 99.9%–100%: no credits
  • 99.5%–99.9%: 5% service credit of monthly invoice
  • 99.0%–99.5%: 15% service credit
  • <99.0%: 30% service credit, escalate to exec review

Concession we can consider: for annual committed spend >= $500k and a 12-month term, we can provide a 10% discount on the premium retainer and tighten P1 remediation to a 4-hour target for Dedicated deployments. We'd want to document the exact observability signals (edge metrics vs customer telemetry) used to measure the SLA. I've attached the internal escalation_playbook_v1.docx for your review.

—Vivek
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Jordan / Vivek —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the playbook. A few follow-ups from procurement and legal: 

- Credits granularity: procurement is asking for per-incident credits measured in 10-minute buckets below the SLO (e.g., 3% credit per 10m below until a cap) rather than broad monthly bands. Is that something you can operationalize?
- For the discount: we need a 20% support-retainer discount in year one to get internal buy-in; otherwise we land at the lower spend band. Can Redwood do 20% for year one, stepping down to 10% in year two?
- Pilot: we'd like a 90-day pilot with a partial commit and an option to convert to Dedicated within that period without penalty.
- Named contacts: can we request a named senior technical contact for the first 30 days during onboarding?

If you can convert this into a redlined SLA we can move legal quickly. We're hoping to finalize pricing by Friday so the board can approve the Q1 implementation window.

—Olivia

Olivia —

Appreciate the clarity from procurement — we've pulled this together into a concise proposal and next-steps so your team can move quickly: 

Summary proposal (high level) —
1) Uptime & credits: keep monthly bands for simplicity but operationalize per-incident measurement for P1 outages. We can convert to 10-minute buckets for P1 credits (3% per 10 min below SLO, capped at 50% of the monthly invoice) — we can include exact measurement methodology in the SLA annex.

2) Support retainer discount: we can offer 20% off the retainer for year one for a 12-month paid commit >= $400k, moving to 10% in year two. For a $300k commit we can accommodate 15% year-one.

3) Pilot agreement: 90-day pilot as requested — pilot is billable at a reduced ramp rate and any committed capacity conversion to Dedicated inside the 90 days converts the pilot spend to committed credit (no penalty).

4) Named contacts and onboarding: we will assign a named senior technical contact for the first 30 days and provide a small onboarding retainer (included in premium retainer).

Next steps: 
- Laura will open a formal quote in HubSpot (deal NB-2026-074) with two price points (400k commit w/20% retainer discount and 300k commit w/15% discount).
- I'll attach the proposed SLA text and MAA for your legal team to review (MAA-v2.pdf).
- If that looks good, Laura and I can schedule a 30-minute legal hand-off on Thursday.

If you want, we can also schedule a short exec call to sign off on the credits ceiling — happy to arrange.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
